hammer_findings.finding: M195 resets pairing inside every token, flushes every odd tail before moving on, and never carries phase through a zero-event token. This is consistent with M184's one-active-token ownership contract, provided RTL does not accept/rearm the next token until the tail and all responses have retired.

Two independent chunk sizes and bit decoders reproduce the aggregate and every stage exactly. Record identity, path-encoded sample/module/call IDs, payload SHA, size, popcount, window count, pair count and tail conservation all close.

For two windows of one token and one output block, merging each physical bank's queues is mathematically legal for linear accumulation: every signed weight term still contributes exactly once to the same Acc24 and addition order is immaterial. The payload DSE retains bank loads, not channel/weight values, so this is a schedule proof rather than an RTL numerical proof.

The reported 1.108968500x excludes token header/done work, all zero-token wall time, finite two-buffer fill/drain, odd-tail release latency, stalls and weight-response latency. It is an exact replay opportunity, not executable or wall-clock speedup.

M186 review evidence already exposes stale-response/reset alias risk. A token phase reset alone cannot protect the new token from an old SRAM response; an epoch/token/request tag or a proved flush quarantine is mandatory.

With only two resident buffers, filling the next pair may serialize behind service of the current pair. A third-buffer option must be measured, not assumed; it is admissible only if finite payload cycles and matched area improve together.
BN2 and residual/ATLIF commit are outside the DSE. Token done must wait for the final Acc24 update and all downstream BN2/residual work, with backpressure and reset boundaries preserved.

p0_before_speedup_admission: Implement finite token-owned pair fill/service/drain RTL and replay all 120 payloads with headers, zero-event tokens, odd tails, arbitrary descriptor/issue/response/result stalls and exact conservation.
Carry an epoch plus token/request identity through SRAM request and response, reject or quarantine stale responses across reset and token rearm, and prove no response can update the wrong Acc24.

Use channel- and output-block-tagged numeric VCS scoreboarding to prove every source weight is accumulated exactly once; pair release requires all 16 logical bank queues empty and no response outstanding.
Do not label 1.108968500x as RTL, physical, complete-FC2, FFN or system speedup until the finite matched implementation closes.
p1_required_for_complete_fc2: Measure dual-buffer versus three-buffer fill overlap on the exact payloads and charge the third buffer, ports and control.

Include header/done and zero-token control cycles; an equal overhead of one, two, four or eight cycles per token would reduce the replay ratio to approximately 1.10109x, 1.09427x, 1.08307x or 1.06712x respectively.
Integrate BN2 and residual/ATLIF commit boundaries, final-token drain, downstream backpressure and reset-epoch behavior.
Report SRAM macro area, access energy and response latency; pre-macro combinational ports are not physical evidence.
